howToRecord: Add one object to `incidents` when an agent (or an assistant session) acts on a fact that was true in an earlier session but had since changed — the third part of churn cost, 'new-hire errors'. Required: id (kebab-case, date-prefixed, unique), date (YYYY-MM-DD, when it happened), kind (see `kinds`), title (one line), summary (what was believed vs what was true), recordedIn (issue number that documented it). Optional: refs (issue/PR numbers involved), rounds (extra agent rounds it cost), notes. `dump_churn.py` validates this file on every refresh and fails the dump workflow on a malformed entry, so a bad edit is caught at refresh time rather than silently dropped from the dashboard.

kinds.stale-lane-state: Acted on an out-of-date belief about the project board's lanes, statuses or gating rules.
kinds.stale-artifact-claim: Asserted something about a published artifact (wheel, formula, tag, release) that a newer publish had already invalidated.
kinds.stale-run-state: Acted on an out-of-date belief about what a workflow run or dispatch had already done, racing the real state.

incidents.title: Acceptance Failed lane sweep ran against a stale view of the lane
incidents.summary: A sweep operated on an out-of-date understanding of the Acceptance Failed lane's contents and hold semantics (items filed there are held until Acceptance Testing drains, per the 2026-08-12 drain-gate decision), so the lane had to be re-established by hand.
incidents.notes: Seeded from the owner's 2026-08-14 churn-cost discussion; see #3776 for the incident list this file was created with.

incidents.title: Stale rc4-wheel claims survived past the publish that invalidated them
incidents.summary: Statements about the rc4 wheel were carried forward from an earlier session after newer release-candidate artifacts had been published, so the claims had to be re-verified and corrected instead of being remembered as current.
incidents.notes: Seeded from the owner's 2026-08-14 churn-cost discussion. This is the failure mode the no-expiry-dated-world-state-claims rule (#3744) exists to prevent.

incidents.title: rc7 dispatch race — action taken against a run state that had already moved
incidents.summary: A dispatch was issued against a believed rc7 state that the real run history had already advanced past, racing the actual state and costing a re-verification round.
incidents.notes: Seeded from the owner's 2026-08-14 churn-cost discussion.
